characters.description: Karen's police commissioner, responsible for public order as the city absorbs displaced Chicago residents. The commissioner accepts Tatiana's offer of outside help and invites the visiting group to a government employees' bowling night.
characters.name: Karen's police commissioner

characters.description: Karen's founder and the master served by the animal-featured visitors whom Tatiana recruits to address unrest among the city's new arrivals.
characters.name: Randidly Ghosthound

characters.description: Randidly's sentient armor. It covers the damaged replacement arm and the painful runes extending from his arm to his shoulder.
characters.name: Sulphur

characters.description: Karen's practical civic leader and Randidly's chief administrator. She recruits an intimidating group of his followers to address unrest among the city's new arrivals.
characters.name: Tatiana

characters.description: Randidly's soulbound companion and an Aether specialist. She is working with Sydney in the Toad world when Randidly receives his first briefing after returning to Earth.
characters.name: Nevaeh

characters.description: A Valkyrie and experienced Earth defender. Together with Hank, she is tracking the controller of a murderous blood avatar that previously attacked Zone One's president.
characters.name: Alana

characters.description: An Earth defender pursuing the controller of a murderous blood avatar alongside Alana after the pair prevented an attack on Zone One's president.
characters.name: Hank Howard

characters.description: An associate of Nevaeh who is with her in the Toad world when they report that the immediate situation there is controlled.
characters.name: Sydney

characters.description: A combat-focused subordinate of Randidly and custodian of Karen's elite order. She brings the captured James Kelly to Karen and challenges Randidly to a spear spar.
characters.name: Helen

characters.description: A former professional basketball player who leads the surviving Chicago Chosen. His karmic network redirects his pain and injuries into his followers.
characters.name: James Kelly

characters.description: Kirstie's twin brother. He joins her and two veteran protectors on a trip to encourage Mariah Jane during her football halftime performance, and believes his ability might help the young archer adopt a singing class.
characters.name: Nathan

characters.description: Nathan's twin sister. She travels with him, Tykes, and Dinesh to encourage Mariah Jane during the singer's scheduled football halftime performance.
characters.name: Kirstie

characters.description: A sixteen-year-old halftime performer with an archer class and a connection to Nathan, who believes his ability might help her pursue a singing-related class.
characters.name: Mariah Jane

characters.description: One of Nathan's experienced protectors. He accompanies Nathan and Kirstie to support Mariah Jane at her scheduled football halftime performance.
characters.name: Dinesh

characters.description: One of Nathan's experienced protectors. He travels with Nathan, Kirstie, and Dinesh to support Mariah Jane at her football halftime performance.
characters.name: Tykes

characters.description: Zone One's president and chairperson of the World Council. She receives a warning of a credible attack on the inaugural football game after Karen's elite order declines to provide guards.
characters.name: Theodora Grayman

characters.description: A Zone One guard assigned to protect and monitor quarterback Jake Tuck during the inaugural football game.
characters.name: Ezekiel

characters.description: The East Providence Stallions quarterback. He aims to make himself and his team the leading public face of the revived football league.
characters.name: Jake Tuck

characters.description: A grievously injured survivor receiving treatment for a chaotic fate. His suffering drives Sydney to seek vengeance against those she considers responsible.
characters.name: Drake

characters.description: An energy surgeon treating Drake with guidance informed by Nathan's advice. She can restrain his chaotic fate but cannot safely remake it.
characters.name: Regina Northwind

characters.description: A widowed Zone One border officer and Timothy's father. He accepts an unfair school ruling rather than risk his son's expulsion, even as the decision further erodes his faith in Zone One's institutions.
characters.name: Derek Moss

characters.description: Derek's son, suspended after striking a well-connected bully. His father accepts an unfair ruling rather than risk Tim's expulsion and remains determined to keep him safe.
characters.name: Timothy Moss

characters.description: Annie's partner and Delilah's father. He joins the ogre-settlement delegation preparing to confront the ruler of the large army beyond the gorge.
characters.name: Dozer

characters.description: Annie and Dozer's daughter, about five years old. She is already trained and armed when Randidly meets her at the ogre settlement.
characters.name: Delilah

characters.description: Dozer's partner and Delilah's mother. She joins the Ogre Gorge group meeting Randidly about the immense army waiting beyond the gorge.
characters.name: Annie

characters.description: A Red Revival representative involved in the concealed operation beneath Zone One's inaugural football game.
characters.name: Declan Hyde

characters.description: Leader of the Earth-bound Nemesai involved in the stadium conspiracy. Her image remains unrestricted, unlike those of her companions.
characters.name: Thea

characters.description: A Red Revival representative coordinating with the Nemesai beneath the stadium. His group plans to slaughter the football crowd and collect their blood for a ritual.
characters.name: Stroud

characters.description: Randidly's living plant spear, carried when he travels to confront the ruler of the Nordon force.
characters.name: Acri

characters.description: Nordon's unnamed three-headed ruler. He sets aside his ceremonial identity and challenges Randidly as the Ogrelord when the floating island arrives above his army.
characters.name: The Ogrelord

characters.description: Randidly's father. He unknowingly holds a required piece of Randidly's fate set, which Randidly can obtain only if his father gives it freely.
characters.name: Randidly's father

characters.description: The power behind Kirstie's priestess abilities, expressed through a hostile treant-like image when she attacks Stroud.
characters.name: Arbor

characters.description: The dragon broodmother Alana rides into the sealed stadium during the defense against the blood ritual and the Nemesai attack.
characters.name: Wyvanya

characters.description: A winged-serpent Nemesai that manifests during the stadium assault and activates the blood-gathering stone-wheel array.
characters.name: The winged-serpent Nemesai

characters.description: The three-headed ogre lord whom Randidly recently defeated. He is identified during the report on the stadium disaster and the enormous ogre migration now approaching Karen.
characters.name: Wolfram

characters.description: Randidly's sea soul seed, an ocean-spanning thorned seaweed organism. Thorn grieves the dead dagger fighter, whom it regarded as its closest relationship outside Randidly.
characters.name: Thorn

characters.description: A dormant remnant within Randidly's Ignition Essence, associated with phoenix power but not yet forming a coherent center for the image.
characters.name: Elim

characters.description: A recruiter for Karen's elite order. Naffer interviews Derek after he and Tim arrive in the city seeking a safer home and a path toward greater strength.
characters.name: Naffer Sweet

characters.description: An ancient enemy using Lyra's appearance. She has spread an Aether territory across the Endless Sea and appears to be preparing a trap as part of an effort to escape the System.
characters.name: The woman wearing Lyra's face

characters.description: The leader whose destructive image maintains discipline among the hunted Nemesai. She regards Randidly's birthday invitation as genuine and sees it as a possible opportunity.
characters.name: Thea Glasshammer

characters.description: A Donnyton representative coordinating its delegation to Randidly's birthday gathering with Donnie and helping select the settlement's gift.
characters.name: Mrs. Hamilton

characters.description: Randidly's Nexus contact, who reports that the Council presented Earth's corrupted-invader scenario as a reward and warns that it carries concealed danger.
characters.name: Octavius Shrike

characters.description: An undead Hero under Nevaeh's care. He attends Randidly's birthday gathering while resenting her control and looking for a chance to escape it.
characters.name: Roy

characters.description: A visitor from the Alpha Cosmos whom Randidly invites to his birthday gathering because her past actions illustrate the System's consequences.
characters.name: Alta Bounty

characters.description: Randidly's former best friend, now pursuing a secretive blood-powered project. He has stolen magical-plastic research, an Impending Rock, and lifeblood essence to construct an egg-like creation.
characters.name: Ace

characters.description: A deceased former enemy appearing in a memory reached through the Dreamcatcher. In that remembered encounter, she tried to appropriate Randidly's images and Aether crossroads for her own refuge.
characters.name: Yestix

characters.description: A Nexus investigator expected to interfere with Earth's corrupted-invader trial. Randidly is warned that the official is stronger than his former military superior and may use the scenario to force Earth into failure.
characters.name: The Zurt Brigade special investigator

characters.description: Ace's ally, who recognizes that his fixation on opposing Randidly is becoming more severe. She remains beside him and admits that they took Yestix's missing memories.
characters.name: Rose Calloway

characters.description: A Karen diplomat and ritual user operating ahead of the moving city. Randidly orders Karen toward her position as a vast bubble-city caravan approaches.
characters.name: Vi

characters.description: Naffer Sweet's partner and Ed Dug's former assistant. She ends her job with Ed and relocates to Karen to join Naffer.
characters.name: Maureen

characters.description: A person known to Randidly whose appearance is being used by the ancient creature spreading Aether through the northern Endless Sea.
characters.name: Lyra

characters.description: The authoritarian leader of a bubble-city caravan numbering nearly half a million people. He approaches Karen after ruling a Moscow suburb harshly and is identified by the Blighted Paragon class.
characters.name: The blighted paragon

characters.description: The Nexus's supreme individual power. He interrupts an emergency council dispute, kills the specialist-force leader, and orders Earth protected because the planet troubles his incomplete memory.
characters.name: The Nexus pinnacle figure

characters.description: A powerful Nexus figure returning after a long absence. Distinct from the deceased woman tied to Yestix, she protects the seventh-cohort overseer from a powerful family's representative and resumes involvement in Randidly's affairs.
characters.name: The returned original woman

recaps.ending: Earth completes the corrupted-invader trial, receives two tier-one Nexus citizenship tokens, and avoids inheriting the invaders' displaced populations and energy burden. The victory is followed by a Great Rift and a Nether rescue offensive aimed at the subdued Nether King supporting the seventh cohort. Randidly, Karen's veterans, Alana, Hank, Helen, and other defenders eliminate the initial surface probes. The Nexus pinnacle figure then orders Earth protected, and a specialist response is due. Earth is spherical again, with a new zone, unstable borderlands, emerging bubble cities, and a runic tablet that can grant a formal Nexus name. Randidly refuses to claim the available token or control the naming contest. He plans to withdraw Karen and his organization from directing Earth, leaving Tatiana and Naffer to strengthen Karen through alliances. His departure for the Nexus must wait until he deals with the disgraced investigator abandoned on Earth and reclaims Yestix's memories from Ace and Rose. The Great Rift is contained but not resolved, Lyra's freedom remains uncertain, and Ace continues building a rival threat.
recaps.in_short: Randidly returns to Earth and a rapidly growing Karen, determined to prepare the planet without ruling it. His restraint contributes to the catastrophic stadium massacre, after which he gathers Earth's powers and coordinates a corrupted-invader trial secretly designed to expose his Nether. He remakes Ignition Essence as the Stillborn Phoenix, neutralizes the investigator's Aether Mines, and breaks a System limit on his body. Earth clears the trial, but a Great Rift opens and sends Nether forces to the surface. Randidly and Earth's defenders destroy the first incursion, while the Nexus's supreme power orders specialists to protect the planet. With Earth transformed and politically exposed, Randidly decides to leave governance to Tatiana, Naffer, and Earth's factions. Before departing for the Nexus, he intends to kill the stranded investigator and recover Yestix's stolen memories from Ace and Rose.

recaps.text: Previously: Randidly Ghosthound became one of Earth's strongest protectors, founded the moving city of Karen, and developed three major images while building an unusual command of both Aether and Nether. His path also drew him into Nexus military service and conflict with powerful families and System authorities. Nevaeh remained his soulbound companion and Aether specialist, while Tatiana managed Karen and allies such as Helen, Alana, and Hank defended Earth. Randidly's old friend Ace moved toward blood-based power and opposition. Several pieces of a fate set remained beyond Randidly's reach. Earth itself was still divided into zones and isolated bubble cities, approaching calamities that would test whether it could survive as part of the wider Nexus. Randidly returned home intending to prepare the planet, but without becoming the ruler on whom every institution depended.

Randidly returns to Earth on six months' leave with a rebuilt left arm and the Philosopher's Key. Karen has absorbed thousands of traumatized Chicago arrivals and become prosperous, mobile, and increasingly tied to his image. He orders the city toward Ogre Gorge while encouraging new transport systems built around its intelligent moss spirits. Several threats remain active: a blood-avatar murderer, a distant hostile creature, and the implications of clearing more danger zones. Randidly declines the World Council's Hero Initiative because it resembles surveillance. Helen then delivers James Kelly, leader of the remaining Chicago Chosen. Kelly transfers pain and injury to his followers, so Randidly uses the Philosopher's Key to sever those karmic connections before killing him. The immediate Chosen threat ends, but Randidly is troubled by the moral cost of his action and by Karen's growing dependence on his power.

Karen prepares to leave its isolation while Randidly tests his growing Nether abilities. Earth clears a fourth danger zone, and Nevaeh learns that the next reward would strengthen Earth by absorbing abandoned System structures at a severe cost to displaced populations. The inaugural football game proceeds despite warnings of an attack. Derek Moss, a disillusioned Zone One officer, takes his suspended son Timothy to attend. Randidly identifies guard Ezekiel as the bearer of the next piece of his fate set but refuses to intervene directly in the game, believing Earth must learn to defend itself. Karen crosses Zone One with a conspicuous display of independence and reaches Ogre Gorge. Nearly half a million outside troops are waiting beyond it, so Randidly, Dozer, Sam, and an ogre leader prepare a small delegation to confront their ruler from Randidly's floating island.

Randidly challenges the three-headed ruler of the outside army and wins their duel through superior strength, Nether pressure, and Acri. At the same time, the football game becomes a coordinated Red Revival and Nemesai massacre. Blood seals trap the crowd, controlled attackers infiltrate the stadium, and a ritual begins collecting the victims' blood. Derek prepares explosives, Kirstie attacks the ritual leaders, Nathan protects the wounded, and Ezekiel fights corrupted bodies. Randidly senses the crisis and dispatches a monstrous duplicate of himself from Nordon. Alana enters on Wyvanya, while other defenders contest the invaders and the released creatures. The duplicate breaks into the sealed stadium and confronts the principal blood mage, whose plan depends on mass death and on using the disaster to shape Earth's image of Randidly.

Randidly's intervention kills the principal blood mage and helps end the stadium ritual, but roughly fourteen thousand people die. The disaster discredits one major order, forces the World Council chair to resign, and leaves the lifeblood accumulation in unreliable hands. Randidly admits that he could have prevented more deaths but maintains that Earth must experience the consequences of its own institutional failures. The decision strengthens his Nether as people assign meaning to his restraint, while survivors struggle to understand why their strongest protector did not save everyone. Randidly then comforts his grieving sea soul seed, Thorn, after the death of its closest human companion. Evidence in the dead fighter's home suggests an outside manipulator deliberately distorted the man's grief with promises linked to another Earth. Randidly postpones that confrontation until he is calmer and turns to training.

Derek and Tim choose to relocate to Karen, where Tim's affinity with moss spirits becomes immediately apparent. Derek applies to Karen's order and evolves from Sylvan Archer into Bombardier of the Sacred Grove, a class shaped by his determination to protect his son. Randidly plans a large birthday gathering as a forum for Earth's leaders, System contacts, and even the Nemesai. Before the event, he investigates the ancient woman using Lyra's face, whose Aether has spread through the Endless Sea. He and Nevaeh break through her territorial defenses and descend into a vast engraved cavern. There they confront an aged version of the woman in a chamber she describes as a tomb. Randidly has spent one of his limited liquid-Aether reserves reaching her, while Nevaeh begins dismantling the surrounding arrays.

The woman wearing Lyra's face appears to be dead. She leaves Randidly a canvas that becomes the third piece of his fate set and a recorded account claiming that her husband created the System around their imprisoned pure-energy son. She asks Randidly to free him, but the memory inheritance she intended to leave is missing, apparently taken by people from Earth. Randidly remains suspicious yet accepts that he is grieving an irreplaceable enemy. Nevaeh stays to study the tomb's vast engraving system. Karen prepares for the birthday gathering, and Derek becomes a defense liaison linking city police, ogres, and Randidly's allied forces. Just before the event, Earth clears its fifth danger zone. The reward opens a corrupted-invader scenario requiring hidden bases to be destroyed before the first calamity, with an epic danger zone promised after success.

Randidly learns that the corrupted-invader scenario is nominally a Nexus reward but likely conceals a threat aimed at him. Karen's birthday gathering brings together Earth's rival powers, visitors from beyond cleared danger zones, and the Nemesai. Tim gains the ability to communicate with Karen's moss spirits and joins other children in trying to enter the celebration. The formal image contest exposes deep divisions and competitive ambitions among the guests. Randidly silences the contest and begins the meeting's central purpose: warning the assembled leaders that Earth has only about two weeks to clear the corrupted bases and face the epic zone. His intention is to coordinate action without allowing Earth's factions to mistake their current strength for readiness to survive the Nexus.

The birthday gathering reveals several personal and strategic developments. Ace is secretly combining stolen research, lifeblood essence, and other materials into an egg-like project that he presents as a gift for Randidly. His secrecy and deteriorating behavior make the project potentially dangerous. Ezekiel freely gives Randidly the Dreamcatcher of the Long Night, the second fate-set piece, which allows him to enter dangerous projections of formative memories. The seventh-cohort overseer explains that a powerful family engineered Earth's corrupted-invader trial and placed a Zurt Brigade investigator in position to interfere. Randidly rejects escape to the Nexus and considers confronting the investigator. He then demonstrates his three images before the party, while the overseer's single image overwhelms many of Earth's strongest attendees. After quantifying how poorly comparable worlds survive their calamities, Randidly reveals the four corrupted danger-zone locations and calls on Earth's factions to cooperate.

Earth's factions form four expeditions to attack the corrupted-invader bases. Randidly offers the winged-serpent Nemesai conditional cooperation and refuses Theodora Grayman's request to help give images to Zone One's constrained raid bosses. He begins using the Dreamcatcher to train against Elim and other memories, strengthening Ignition Essence while discovering that Nether use inside the projections can cause real harm. His expanding Nether nebula proves more suppressive than his Aether, though difficult to conceal. Alana negotiates a home for her frost-dragon allies and confirms Hank as her partner. Randidly finally traces the missing memories from the seaside tomb to Ace and Rose. Ace escapes through blood-based movement, but Rose admits that they took the memories. Randidly warns her that any misuse will bring retaliation, leaving the theft as an unresolved personal conflict.

Randidly and Nevaeh flatten his outward Nether into a discreet, self-sustaining field. Karen moves toward diplomat Vi and an approaching bubble-city caravan while its leaders continue expanding political and technical relationships. Lyra reconciles with Randidly and warns that the special investigator intends to attack an Earth task force, but Randidly recognizes that her message was coerced and designed to lure him into a dungeon trap. Seeking enough power to survive the coming confrontation, he uses Dreamcatcher advice to remake the incomplete Ignition Essence. Its inspiration, inherited despair, and phoenix legacy become the Stillborn Phoenix, a concealed black-hole-like pinnacle image with new gravitational and destructive techniques. The investigator's coercion of Lyra and intention to kill Randidly are then confirmed, while the corrupted-invader expeditions continue advancing.

Randidly uses Nevaeh as an illusionary decoy and confronts the special investigator outside the intended dungeon trap. The investigator suspects him of serving Nether but lacks immediate grounds to attack, so both sides prepare for the epic danger zone. Dreamcatcher simulations show Randidly that obvious Nether use lets the investigator isolate him from Earth and drain his strongest advantage. The Swak family also seeks to place another watcher near him. Earth suffers few losses as its task forces advance, and Randidly continues withholding Karen's veterans so local powers develop their own images. When the first corrupted base falls, four Aether Mines activate around Randidly. They inflict escalating pain and threaten to force the detectable Nether response that the investigator needs as evidence. The epic zone's probable location also becomes clear.

The Aether Mines tighten their trap while Randidly searches for a response that will not expose his Nether. Elsewhere, Karen confronts a caravan of nearly half a million people led by the blighted paragon. Diplomat Vi defeats and humiliates the authoritarian leader, dispersing his followers and allowing Karen to absorb selected refugees. Ace takes an interest in the paragon's cellular alteration as material for his rival creation. Randidly turns the mines' punishment into physical training, discovering a spectral barrier that limits what his body can express. With Nevaeh sharing the mental burden and analyzing the devices, he uses non-skill physical force to make the four mines lock together and go inert. The investigator does not immediately react, indicating that the neutralization has escaped notice and giving Randidly two days to pursue his bodily breakthrough.

Randidly tears away the System-imposed limit on his physical body. The System warns that his development contradicts its preferred image-based path and gives him six hours to accept repair or lose its energy, but he refuses. The winged-serpent Nemesai secures neutrality from its people, making future cooperation conditional on Earth's success. Randidly orders Alana and Hank to clear the final corrupted base and places Helen in command of the epic-zone force. Earth completes both operations, gains additional energy and two tier-one Nexus citizenship tokens, and ends the corrupted-invader trial without the investigator appearing. The apparent victory immediately becomes a larger emergency when a dark Great Rift forms above Earth, surrounded by failing Aether structures and carrying a powerful concentration of Nether.

The Great Rift is a Nether rescue offensive aimed at the subdued Nether King supporting the seventh cohort. The special investigator is recalled too late, stripped of rank, and abandoned on Earth, still planning to expose Randidly. Nether probes reach the surface, but Randidly kills their Gatekeeper outside Franksburg while Karen's veterans, Alana, Hank, Helen, and other defenders eliminate the remaining incursions. The Nexus pinnacle figure kills a resistant specialist leader and orders Earth protected. Earth becomes spherical again, gains a new zone, and faces unstable borderlands, bubble cities, and a contest over a runic tablet that can name the planet. Randidly refuses to control that contest or take the available citizenship token. He tells Tatiana that Karen and his organization will withdraw from directing Earth, leaving her and Naffer to build alliances. He plans to enter the Nexus after killing the stranded investigator and recovering Yestix's memories from Ace and Rose.

characters.description: A member of the Swak family whom Randidly is preparing to confront while his damaged left arm is failing. The approaching Zurt Brigade prevents Randidly from moving against him immediately.
characters.name: Khan Swak

characters.description: Randidly's soulbound partner is an Aether and engraving specialist. She studies Yestix's living engravings in hopes of helping him replace his damaged arm, and she can conceal her bone-worm identity with an illusion.
characters.name: Nevaeh

characters.description: Karen's founder and Earth's protector begins this volume under pressure from several directions. He is training Yggdrasil, the Stillborn Phoenix, and the Grim Chimera to act through one body, while his damaged metal left arm is failing and a major Nether assault threatens Earth.
characters.name: Randidly Ghosthound

characters.description: A visibly troubled Nemesai who arrives with a winged serpent under an agreement with Randidly. Thea helps deliver a mysterious weapon while showing fear, anger, and envy after her time away.
characters.name: Thea Glasshammer

characters.description: The creator of a body of living-engraving work that Nevaeh is studying. Randidly needs to understand this material before it can help improve his failing arm.
characters.name: Yestix

characters.description: A winged serpent that arrives with Thea Glasshammer under the Nemesai agreement and brings Randidly a mysterious weapon.
characters.name: Winged serpent

characters.description: Randidly's eager living spear is sent away to kill powerful monsters and gather their bones for his replacement arm. Acri is both a weapon and an active companion capable of pursuing a task independently.
characters.name: Acri

characters.description: A figure whose living status is a central source of doubt for Thea. She rejects Randidly’s assurance that Chrysanthemum is alive.
characters.name: Chrysanthemum

characters.description: A trusted offworld combat leader whom Randidly leaves visible when the Zurt Brigade inspects Earth. Her presence helps his preparations appear ordinary while his other offworld associates remain concealed.
characters.name: Helen

characters.description: Randidly's contact in the Zurt Brigade. She advises him on how to handle the visiting investigators and warns him to appear unexceptional before the ambitious Smog Clan captain.
characters.name: Octavia Shrike

characters.description: The Smog Clan commander leads the Zurt Brigade inspection force on Earth. Captain Quill establishes a temporary command center on Randidly's island while his forces complete their work.
characters.name: Captain Quill

characters.description: Captain Quill's gray-skinned aide and a skilled evaluator of engravings. Wuva accompanies Quill when the Zurt Brigade establishes its temporary base on Randidly's island.
characters.name: Wuva

characters.description: A guard at Zone 1's restricted Mjolnir facility. His shift creates the opening Acri uses to enter the complex and reach its large stock of monster cores, placing him at the edge of Randidly's effort to build a replacement arm.
characters.name: Kale

characters.description: An Order Dukies applicant whose combat class is suited to clearing groups of monsters. Derek helps welcome survivors recruited for Karen and explains that citizenship brings demanding training and a duty to defend other people.
characters.name: Derek Moss

characters.description: Derek Moss's mentor in the Order Dukies. Naffer presents the order as a way for ordinary people to build strength of their own.
characters.name: Naffer

characters.description: Karen's civic leader manages the city's shortages of space, teachers, industry coordination, and predictable travel. She gives Randidly room to set broad priorities while preparing to turn his ambitious expansion ideas into workable administration.
characters.name: Tatiana

characters.description: A long-incapacitated fighter under Sydney’s care. He has suffered severe pain for nearly a year, and Sydney remains at his bedside.
characters.name: Drake

characters.description: Firun relentlessly hunts the Nemesai after their interference almost sent Ifran into the sea.
characters.name: Firun

characters.description: Naffer's prospective wife. Maureen asks Randidly to approve their marriage because she regards him as a father figure in Naffer's life.
characters.name: Maureen

characters.description: Drake's protector and Ace's former partner cares for Drake through a long, unexplained incapacitation. When Thea tries to provoke her, Sydney suppresses her anger with a cold image and refuses the offered fight.
characters.name: Sydney

characters.description: A paralyzed Zone 1 fighter following a deviant path. Nether use has left him in continual pain, but he remains involved in the president's plan to infiltrate and betray a joint expedition for control of a runic tablet.
characters.name: Richter

characters.description: Zone 1's president is under impeachment pressure when she orders Nether-using subordinates to join an expedition, betray its allies, and seize a runic tablet. Her decision presents political survival as worth a planned attack on rival forces.
characters.name: Theodora Grayman

characters.description: Randidly's former friend possesses Yestix's stolen memories even though they reject his attempts to use them. He is also cultivating an immense fleshy egg fed by negative emotion, making his hidden work an urgent danger.
characters.name: Ace Ridge

characters.description: A highly influential child in Karen whose inherited Aether connection helps her lead other children. Tatiana compares Delilah's influence among the young to the authority Randidly carries among adults.
characters.name: Delilah

characters.description: Karen’s committed chief of police. Commissioner Arrietty reports that public interest in joining the Order Dukies has increased after refugees witnessed the order fighting.
characters.name: Commissioner Arrietty

characters.description: An undead Hero living under Nevaeh's care. Something experienced while dead has left Roy disturbingly resigned, and his refusal to discuss the change makes his passive obedience more troubling to her.
characters.name: Roy

characters.description: An engraving specialist whom Randidly recruits to help guide the development of Karen Academy.
characters.name: Lucretia

characters.description: Donington's absent village spirit has not been seen for several weeks. Her unexplained disappearance matters to Randidly as he checks the people and places he may leave behind when he travels to the Nexus.
characters.name: Lyra

characters.description: An engineer who examines Randidly's failed metallic arm and advises how it might be reinforced. She also provides technical guidance for the developing Karen Academy.
characters.name: Wendy

characters.description: A Zurt Brigade investigator intent on proving that Randidly is a Nether agent. He enters Randidly's prepared enclosure, deploys a suppression space, and isolates his target from both Nevaeh and the Nether power on which the trap depends.
characters.name: Zurt Brigade special investigator

characters.description: Ace's collaborator watches Randidly's preparations with him and helps ready the large egg intended to disrupt the coming confrontation.
characters.name: Ezekiel

characters.description: A spear fighter who responds to the recent destructive battle by training harder. Alana decides Earth must develop defenders who do not depend on Randidly and prepares to enter his duos tournament with a powerful partner.
characters.name: Alana

characters.description: Alana's frost-dragon partner and a broodmother. Wyvanya urges Alana to enter the duos tournament with her and already has a preferred name for Earth if they win the naming tablet that serves as its prize.
characters.name: Wyvanya

characters.description: Ace's grieving former second-in-command is digging his grave when Randidly finds her. An observant analyst with broad skill knowledge, Rose helps bury Ace and then asks Randidly to give her useful work.
characters.name: Rose Calloway

characters.description: A provisional Karen investigator whose passive image worsens surrounding circumstances when her emotions slip. Heidi works with Derek to examine an attempted killing, using the violent image traces left at the scene.
characters.name: Heidi Mordath

characters.description: The injured owner of a bagel shop and the witness in Derek and Heidi's investigation of an attempted killing. Gary exaggerates how well he resisted the attack, while the image traces show that he was nearly killed.
characters.name: Gary Dietz

characters.description: Derek's young son has a rare affinity with Karen's moss spirits and an ability that seems to teach him image use naturally. Randidly considers whether Timothy could learn the specialized engraving needed to create permanent floating islands.
characters.name: Timothy Moss

characters.description: A contact whose advice Randidly awaits while considering a dungeon as a place to train his unstable images.
characters.name: Octavius

characters.description: Randidly's offworld contact is mentally depleted while undergoing severe training. Their secret Nether Ritual allows him to reach her.
characters.name: Vuala

characters.description: An experienced construction professional whom Randidly recruits to advise the Karen Academy project.
characters.name: Ed Doug

characters.description: The first Karen citizenship applicant to complete the image challenge is also an accomplished educator. Gertrude can hold the attention of more than a hundred children with simple illusions shaped by clear motives.
characters.name: Gertrude Collins

characters.description: An elite smith with a longstanding friendship and Aether bond to Randidly. Sam agrees to support Karen Academy's specialized construction in exchange for the first human expedition to a corrupted world.
characters.name: Sam

characters.description: An Academy worker who joins Randidly's planned six-month dungeon expedition. Dinesh is part of the mixed contingent using the isolated space for combat training, construction, and institutional planning.
characters.name: Dinesh

characters.description: A combat trainer assigned alongside Helen to prepare Karen's police force during its six-month dungeon expedition.
characters.name: Ajax

characters.description: The memory portrays this figure as the System's creator and as having once been married to the woman who appears with Lyra's face. He uses runes to keep her pure-energy child intact, then confines that being as the System's power source.
characters.name: Aether historian

characters.description: This unnamed being was born from a union between a Nether King and the woman who resembles Lyra. The Aether historian prevents his energy from dispersing, but holds him captive to power the System. Records sealed on Halom could help Nevaeh devise a rescue.
characters.name: Pure-energy son

characters.description: Appearing with Lyra's face, this woman says the historian was once her husband. She directs Randidly toward sealed records on Halom that could help Nevaeh release her confined son.
characters.name: Woman wearing Lyra's face

characters.description: Delilah's father reacts protectively when she reports that a boy named Anon claimed she loved him.
characters.name: Dozer

characters.description: Donington’s leader enters the duos tournament with Glendal, whose captured raid-boss spirits overwhelm opponents during their desert preliminary.
characters.name: Donington’s leader

characters.description: Hank Howard's horse and his declared tournament partner. Ancho is not presented as a conventional combatant, but his place in Hank's identity is essential to the marksman's image and to the partnership they bring into the contest.
characters.name: Ancho

characters.description: Donington’s ghost-using tournament partner. Glendal deploys captured raid-boss spirits against opponents in a desert preliminary.
characters.name: Glendal

characters.description: A marksman who enters the duos tournament with his ordinary horse rather than a conventional fighter. Hank treats Ancho as an inseparable part of his gunslinger image, making their partnership more substantial than it first appears.
characters.name: Hank Howard

characters.description: Dinesh’s tournament partner first appears opposite Lyra and her unresponsive partner in a mist-filled preliminary. Their opening confrontation begins as Lyra clears the mist during her exchange with Tykes.
characters.name: Tykes

characters.description: Lyra's living tournament partner is physically present during the mist-filled preliminary but remains unresponsive when Dinesh addresses him.
characters.name: Stan

characters.description: A tournament fighter who competes alongside Kale under a wager that has them exchange their usual weapons.
characters.name: Paolo

characters.description: A concealed tournament identity paired with Richter and listed among the projected semifinalists. The person behind the title is not yet established.
characters.name: Black Hand

characters.description: Lucifer’s tournament partner and one of the contestants identified during a live broadcast as a projected semifinalist.
characters.name: Juliana

characters.description: Juliana's tournament partner and one of the contestants identified during a live broadcast as a projected semifinalist.
characters.name: Lucifer

characters.description: An adopted member of the Huang family who serves as Zone 7’s royal-guard captain. He prepares to enter the tournament alongside an older adoptive relative despite political strain between them.
characters.name: Zone 7 captain

characters.description: The Zone 7 captain’s older adoptive relative and tournament partner. This politically influential elder joins him as they prepare to compete despite strain between them.
characters.name: Elderly Zone 7 partner

characters.description: Black Hand is revealed as the impeached former president Theodora Grayman. She has converted more of her body into a source of caustic Nether power for the tournament fight, exposing the connection between the political figure and the masked combatant.
characters.name: Black Hand

characters.description: Zone 7's captain and Huang Shou's adoptive grandson. After reaching the tournament quarterfinals, he struggles with contamination in his wounded image and the prospect of facing Paolo and Kale.
characters.name: Huang Li

characters.description: Huang Li's adoptive grandfather and tournament partner. He identifies the foreign influence destabilizing Huang Li's wounded image and redirects him toward confidence in his accumulated effort.
characters.name: Huang Shou

characters.description: The crab-mutated owner of an isolated villa operates banks and lending businesses whose influence has reached Karen through their customers. Randidly confronts him while assessing social pressures that could threaten the city after his departure.
characters.name: Villa owner

characters.description: The drain is Vuala's new identity after she gives up her former Nexus citizenship. She needs active-cohort citizenship coins from Randidly to pursue Tier Three standing and a civilian position on the Nexus Council.
characters.name: Drain

characters.description: Donington’s leader, now identified as Donnie, partners with Glendal in the duos tournament. Their defensive effort is overcome by Tykes and Dinesh in the fight for a semifinal place.
characters.name: Donnie

characters.description: Randidly's official guide meets him at a crowded relay after his arrival in the Nexus. The overseer bypasses the ordinary queue and begins escorting him toward the Nexus proper, giving him his first direct contact there.
characters.name: Seventh-cohort overseer

characters.description: An independent artificial intelligence whose concealed production operation Randidly moves to the former winged-serpent island. In return for a future favor from Randidly or Nevaeh, it agrees to aid Karen as many as three times and remain available through the city's calamities.
characters.name: Independent AI

characters.description: One of Randidly's original soul seeds, now sufficiently independent that he advises Arbor to choose a purposeful life of its own.
characters.name: Arbor

characters.description: One of Randidly's original soul seeds, now acting independently. Thorn intends to root at Xperia's center and protect its people.
characters.name: Thorn

characters.description: A dangerous older near-double of Vuala whom Randidly meets in the Nexus Undercity. Her exact relationship to Vuala is not explained when she offers him a position as a military drill sergeant in an emergency program.
characters.name: Original Vuala

characters.description: A frontline military leader allied with the original Vuala's faction. She arranges Randidly's tribunal interview and instructs him to display only the controlled healing aspect of Yggdrasil before the divided panel.
characters.name: Military woman

characters.description: A Zurt Brigade investigator on the Nexus tribunal that tests Randidly's image control and suitability for military command. At the investigator's request, Randidly works around the room's wards to manifest a physical tree. The investigator then abstains from the initial decision.
characters.name: Nexus Zurt Brigade investigator

characters.description: A senior Nexus military authority who maims a Swak-family applicant for insubordination. Wick then makes Randidly's reconsideration for head drill sergeant conditional on healing the injured applicant.
characters.name: Commandant Wick

characters.description: A metallic applicant from the Swak family whom Commandant Wick maims for insubordination. Wick makes healing the applicant the condition for reconsidering Randidly’s candidacy.
characters.name: Metallic Swak-family applicant

characters.description: An energy reader in a deep-Web household who gives Randidly three territory coins as insurance against failure. The organizer brings together people who want to change how the Nexus treats lives and worlds.
characters.name: Residential household organizer

recaps.ending: Earth is officially named Xperia and faces its first Nexus calamity in 150 days. Karen continues as a mobile city under Tatiana, with its council, Academy plans, elite order, and expansion still developing. Nevaeh remains there to work on engravings and recover from trauma, while Alana and Wyvanya pursue an independent public mission. Xperia's strongest fighters are still recovering from the Nether Randidly took after their test. Randidly and Helen reach the Nexus. After healing a Swak-family applicant whom Commandant Wick maimed, Randidly becomes head drill sergeant and must report in six days, although he has already refused to sacrifice recruits merely to obey an order. Vuala remains entangled in Nexus politics, and the relationship between her and the original Vuala is unresolved. Randidly also joins the seventh-cohort overseer, the military woman, and a deep-Web organizer in a covert reform coalition. He holds three territory coins as a contingency, and the group intends to seek the sealed body of a former Nexus power as leverage against the existing order.
recaps.in_short: Randidly eliminates three immediate threats by killing Khan Swak and a Zurt Brigade investigator, while Sydney kills Ace. He then commits to leaving Karen able to govern, educate, expand, and defend itself without him. A vast duos tournament ends with Alana and Wyvanya defeating Paolo and Kale, naming Earth Xperia, and triggering a calamity deadline of 150 days. Recovered memories attribute the System's creation to an Aether historian who imprisoned a pure-energy being, while Randidly learns that the System strips significance from human memories. Xperia's leading fighters test Randidly in a coordinated ambush, lose, and surrender much of their Nether. Tatiana takes charge of Karen, Nevaeh and Alana remain on Xperia, and Randidly travels with Helen to the Nexus. There he heals a military victim, becomes head drill sergeant, refuses unquestioning obedience, and joins a covert coalition seeking enough power to reform the Nexus.

recaps.text: Previously: Randidly Ghosthound became Karen's founder and Earth's protector while growing into a power capable of attracting dangerous Nexus attention. His strength rests on three principal images - Yggdrasil, the Stillborn Phoenix, and the Grim Chimera - as well as his command of Aether and the forbidden realm of Nether. Nevaeh remains his soulbound partner and an expert in Aether and engraving. Their discoveries in Yestix's legacy suggest that the accepted history of the System and the conflict between Aether and Nether is incomplete. Randidly also carries obligations beyond Earth, including a promise connected to threatened Nemesai worlds and a secret link to Vuala. At the start of this volume, Earth has not yet entered the Nexus under an official name. Karen depends heavily on Randidly, and he expects to leave for the Nexus soon. His former relationships with Sydney and Ace remain damaged, and Drake is incapacitated. A Zurt Brigade presence and the Swak family remain immediate threats.

Randidly tries to manifest Yggdrasil, the Stillborn Phoenix, and the Grim Chimera through one body, but their unequal growth makes the combination unstable. His damaged metal arm is failing just as a Nether assault and the Zurt Brigade converge on Earth. A winged serpent delivers a one-use Nemesai weapon whose true operation remains uncertain, while Nevaeh studies both the weapon and Yestix's living engravings. Randidly conceals most offworld people before Captain Quill's inspection and sends Acri to gather monster bones for a new arm. Karen's growth creates shortages of land, teachers, and civic structure, so Randidly sketches a council, new floating islands, and a large Academy. Sydney continues caring for the incapacitated Drake and refuses Thea's attempt to provoke a fight. Meanwhile, Theodora Grayman orders Richter's group to betray allies during a runic-tablet expedition. Randidly discovers Ace holding Yestix's stolen memories and nurturing a huge fleshly egg. He turns from observation toward direct action against Khan Swak while beginning the dangerous forging of his replacement arm.

Randidly and Nevaeh complete a self-repairing replacement arm from monster bone, rust steel, blood, and living engraving. They then use a brief display of Nether and an isolation barrier to lure the Zurt Brigade special investigator into a trap. The investigator instead seals Randidly inside a suppression space and progressively tunes six pyramids to counter his images. Nevaeh breaches the false space, restoring his Nether and joining the battle, but the investigator uses his fate to overwhelm her with loneliness. Randidly creates an unstable gray pseudo-penance from opposing Nether currents, breaks free, and links his three principal images so they can cover one another's weaknesses. He disrupts the investigator's certainty and kills him with Acri. Elsewhere, Ace prepares to use his blood egg, but Sydney reaches his camp and opposes him. By the end of the battle, the investigator is dead, Randidly is exhausted, his new arm is damaged, and Nevaeh remains mentally destabilized.

Randidly kills Khan Swak and reaches the confrontation between Sydney and Ace too depleted to control it. Sydney rejects Ace's excuses for his violence and kills him, while the enormous blood egg becomes quiet but remains a possible danger. She ends her personal relationship with Randidly and allows only professional contact. Randidly recovers Yestix's stolen memories, though their full contents remain inaccessible, and helps Rose Calloway bury Ace before offering the grieving analyst work. He then accepts that Karen's future cannot be built through sporadic intervention. He announces a duos tournament whose winners will receive the tablet that names Earth, and commits to a council, new islands, and Karen Academy as his legacy. Alana and Wyvanya enter the tournament because Earth needs defenders independent of him. Randidly recruits Timothy Moss to learn permanent floating-island engraving, gives Wendy responsibility for Academy architecture, and arranges dungeon training for his own unstable three-image manifestation. Completing a major visualization path strengthens his conviction and clears the way for that training.

Karen's rapid growth exposes weaknesses in its law, policing, immigration, and education. Derek Moss and Heidi investigate a politically suspicious attempted killing, while Delilah discovers that disciplined students can defeat her natural talent. Randidly reconnects with Vuala through a secret Nether ritual and restores some of the courage stripped away by her offworld training. He expands the Academy design to serve thousands of children and recruits Gertrude Collins, an educator who insists that the institution address child welfare and its ethical purpose. A mixed expedition of police, children, builders, and Academy workers prepares for a long dungeon stay. Nevaeh completes more of Yestix's engraving work but decides she will not accompany Randidly to the Nexus. The investigator's attack has traumatized her, and her comparative advantage lies in Earth-based research. At the same time, Theodora Grayman's impeachment proceeds and she turns toward a final gamble with Richter's corrosive experiments.

Inside a time-distorted dungeon, Randidly trains Karen's police and pushes his three-image body toward stable movement and combat. Helen develops her domain while challenging him, the children build under practical instruction, and the Academy gains hundreds of teachers from the Alpha Cosmos. Derek and Heidi prove effective at detecting manipulated entrants to Karen. Both donate memories to Randidly's Dreamcatcher, gaining greater control and places in Karen's elite order. Delilah receives three skills from an unidentified woman, leaving her benefactor unresolved. After six dungeon months, Randidly can normally manage three images at once and returns only hours after leaving. He then enters Yestix's degraded historical memory. It presents an old Aether society, its conflict with Nether, and an Aether historian who used Nether methods to reshape his people. The account alleges that the historian imprisoned the pure-energy son of a woman wearing Lyra's face and a Nether King, using him to create the System. The memory asks Randidly to seek sealed records and a possible means of freeing the captive being, but the account remains unverified.

Twenty thousand duos enter Randidly's tournament. The preliminary environments quickly expose hidden powers and reduce the field, while Randidly uses the event to promote disciplined image development rather than dependence on him. Hank competes with his horse Ancho, Alana fights beside Wyvanya, Lyra enters with her unresponsive partner Stan, and Tykes pairs with Dinesh. Paolo and Kale remain formidable despite a wager forcing them to exchange weapons. Thea's infernal bear refuses to fight, and Randidly tells her it may truly be dead rather than consciously rejecting her. Karen uses the tournament's pause to recruit more specialists, and Randidly concludes the city's collective image has become diverse rather than merely an extension of his own. He also improves his transformed body and continues seeking a controlled, class-like structure for Nether. The bracket reaches its last sixty-four teams, but Randidly judges Earth's strength sufficient only for its earliest calamity.

Randidly traces a subtle influence on Karen to a banker whose image encourages acceptance of fixed human nature. He warns that Karen will resist the harm such acceptance can excuse, but does not treat the banker as an immediate enemy. In the tournament, Zone 7's captain and his adoptive grandfather face Richter and the masked Black Hand. Richter's corrosive manifestation conceals a dark entity in his legs, while Black Hand is revealed as the impeached Theodora Grayman. She sacrifices more of her body to channel Nether, but Randidly prevents the captain's uncontrolled counterattack from killing her. The Zone 7 pair advances, reducing the tournament field to eight duos.

Paolo and Kale defeat Huang Li and Huang Shou after Kale's precise dividing image destroys Huang Li's stronger but less controlled dragon technique. Tykes and Dinesh advance through a coordinated combination, while Alana and Wyvanya, Hank and Ancho, and Lyra's team continue through the bracket. Randidly learns that Vuala has surrendered her former citizenship and now uses the identity Drain. She needs active-cohort citizenship coins to seek political standing, while reports describe a fragmented Nexus facing expanding Nether attacks. After Hank eliminates Lyra, she invites Randidly to dinner. Lyra argues that images may be a human power rather than a gift of the System and announces her own plan to enter the Nexus, gather allies, and protect Earth by a path different from Randidly's pursuit of individual strength. Randidly commits himself to surpassing the maker of the Nexus. Their paths remain separate, but he recognizes her isolation and wishes her success.

Karen's first representative selection survives attempted disruption, and its new council adopts rules protecting eligibility and removal before setting the city's itinerary. In the tournament semifinals, Tykes and Dinesh merge their images into a reflective battlefield, but Paolo and Kale identify its damage-transfer weakness and win. Alana and Wyvanya then face Hank and Ancho. Alana expands her fire-based revelations until they suppress both Hank's Wild West and Wyvanya's cold. Hank answers with his strongest prepared shots and an image-version of Ancho, but Alana and Wyvanya claim the second berth in the final. Randidly recognizes that Alana's power draws upon an idealized public image of him rather than his actual identity. The championship pairing is set: Alana and Wyvanya against Paolo and Kale. Karen, meanwhile, is beginning to act as a self-directed travelling city rather than an extension of Randidly's decisions.

Hank and Ancho secure third place. In the final, Alana and Wyvanya establish their image first, while Paolo absorbs the audience's support and Kale shapes dividing barriers around him. Wyvanya suffers catastrophic wounds intercepting Kale's attack, and Randidly removes her for treatment. Alone and badly injured, Alana develops a fifth revelation founded on her own desire rather than an assigned role. She maims Paolo and outlasts Kale's final defense. Paolo concedes when his reliance on a challenger's spectral hand proves to him that he has lost. Alana and Wyvanya win the tournament and use the tablet to name Earth Xperia, formally entering it into the Nexus. The reward immediately carries a cost: the System schedules Xperia's first great calamity in 150 days and raises its difficulty because of the world's dense Aether. Randidly plans to finish Karen's projects and depart, but an unexplained rise in significance makes him expect another near-term event.

Vuala reports that recent Nether activity was a feint covering the destruction of multiple Nexus citizen planets. On Xperia, Karen resumes its journey and advances its Academy, farming, housing, policing, and elite-order projects. Randidly subjects the Grim Chimera to repeated Dreamcatcher defeats, forcing it to rebuild around the ember of a destroyed world and its drive to survive. Acri is reforged into a smaller, denser form. Tatiana interrupts this punishing training long enough to make Randidly settle essential plans before leaving. When he arrives for a dinner, Alana initiates a coordinated surprise attack. Randidly is exhausted and limits himself to the Grim Chimera as the challenge begins.

The assembled fighters bind, shoot, cut, and transport Randidly through a prepared sequence, eventually moving the battle into open air for a cloud-dragon strike. Their real aim is to measure how far Xperia's best stand below him and what strength the Nexus will demand. Randidly recognizes the challenge as an attempt at equality rather than murder. Though exhausted and restricted to the Grim Chimera, he adapts through each wound, drains mental energy from several opponents, and survives the combined finishing attack. Alana changes her fate after accepting that she cannot follow his path as a fighter. Randidly defeats Paolo, Lyra, and the remaining combatants, and Alana surrenders for the group. He wins the voluntary test, proving that Xperia's strongest coalition remains below even his limited state.

As punishment for the ambush, Randidly takes seventy percent of each attacker's Nether. Their injuries are not permanent, but Xperia's leading fighters will need weeks to recover while the calamity approaches. He then tells Tatiana he is leaving that night and credits her with making him unnecessary to Karen's government. Karen continues toward the final zone under its new institutions. Alana chooses to remain on Xperia and pursue an independent prophetic role, while Wyvanya expands the memorial complex devoted to Randidly. Nevaeh also stays behind, both for engraving work and because Roy's suicide and the Nexus's amassed significance have left her unwilling to go. Lyra grants Randidly a Tier One citizenship coin and access to the Nexus Ways. Travelling with Helen, he reaches a vast Nexus relay and meets the seventh-cohort overseer, who becomes his official guide toward the Nexus proper.

The overseer guides Randidly through the polluted Aether of the Nexus Undercity and its cable-filled Web. There he meets the original Vuala, a dangerous older near-double whose exact relationship to Vuala remains unknown. Her faction offers him a drill-sergeant position in an emergency program created by spreading Nether taint and war. Randidly is considered for command of privileged recruits, but a divided tribunal initially rejects him. He returns to the deep Web and trains all three images amid stronger Aether, Nether, and time distortion. Political deadlock brings him back when Commandant Wick maims a Swak-family applicant and makes healing the victim his test. Randidly removes Wick's hostile image fragments, rebuilds a serviceable body, and accepts responsibility for the remaining recovery. When Wick asks whether he will obey an order that endangers his charges, Randidly refuses. Wick nevertheless appoints him head drill sergeant, with his new assignment beginning at the fifth cohort station six days later.

Randidly returns briefly to the Web, where the Stillborn Phoenix releases refined emotions and his images continue learning to cooperate. In a deep-Web household, an energy-reading organizer gives him three territory coins as insurance. The coins could remove an entire planet as territory, offering a possible last resort for Xperia or another world tied to his promises. Randidly meets with the organizer, the seventh-cohort overseer, and the military woman who supported his candidacy. Their motives differ, but all reject the Nexus's treatment of lives as expendable resources. Randidly wants people to be free and capable of becoming strong, the overseer wants peace and fewer losses, and the military woman wants to protect those to whom she made promises. They form a covert reform coalition and agree to pursue the sealed body of a former Nexus power as a possible weapon against the entrenched order. Randidly ends the book as head drill sergeant, due to report in six days, while secretly joining a much larger challenge to the Nexus.

characters.description: A powerful image user who accepts command of an elite Fifth Cohort recruit program. He also joins a long-term effort to challenge the Nexus order by exploiting the sealed body of its creator, a plan that first requires military leverage, citizenship, and further research.
characters.name: Randidly Ghosthound

characters.description: The military authority behind Randidly's appointment as head drill sergeant for the Fifth Cohort recruit program.
characters.name: Commandant Wick

characters.description: A veteran lieutenant who joins Randidly and his frontline soldiers for training in the Nexus web.
characters.name: Helen

characters.description: A Wick-family recruit assigned to enter Randidly's elite program, befriend him, and cultivate his loyalty to her family.
characters.name: Charlotte Wick

characters.description: Randidly's soulbound engraving partner, consulted from afar while he designs the elite recruits' specialized training chambers. Her technical advice helps him build an isolated compound whose secrets can be destroyed after use.
characters.name: Nevaeh

characters.description: A foxlike recruit entering the Fifth Cohort program to search for his missing younger brother and help an Aether-starved homeworld.
characters.name: Foxlike recruit

characters.description: The two-tailed fox-person previously seen among Randidly's elite recruits. Raymond is searching for his missing brother, shows unusual physical ability, and helps an exhausted recruit despite his own fatigue.
characters.name: Raymond

characters.description: Randidly's offworld partner and a formidable Fifth Cohort combatant. She is preparing to deploy with a brigade against the Nether offensive, and Randidly regards her as exceptionally difficult to kill despite his concern about the worsening front.
characters.name: Vuala

characters.description: Charlotte's quiet, analytical companion in the elite cohort. He studies the changing flow of Randidly's Nether formation, recognizes how it concentrates and disperses through individual recruits, and receives guidance in focus and image control.
characters.name: Benjamin Rex

characters.description: A rogue Nether ruler whose offensive has breached parts of the Nexus Ways, silenced reclaimed worlds, and killed a Commandant. The growing emergency turns Randidly's elite training project into preparation for imminent frontline service.
characters.name: Nether King

characters.description: A senior military officer who directs security for a commandant's funeral. She belongs to Randidly's alliance seeking to change the leadership of the Nexus.
characters.name: Security chief

characters.description: A prominent member of the Rex family who secretly wields Nether with greater skill than Randidly believes he possesses.
characters.name: Rex-family woman

characters.description: An overseer who keeps physical records of the seventh cohort's Aether harvests and belongs to Randidly's alliance. Intruders immobilize and torture him while demanding those records.
characters.name: Seventh-cohort overseer

characters.description: A hostile ram-horned trainee who can manifest weapons from his body. His self-destructive image and reliance on physical movement undermine his control, so Helen assigns corrective meditation and image training.
characters.name: Ram-demon recruit

characters.description: An exceptionally powerful veteran carrying a runic greatsword. A Swak-family contractor hires him to assess Randidly, and he accepts after witnessing Randidly travel by portal without the Nexus Ways.
characters.name: Tattooed swordsman

characters.description: A demigod who addresses Raymond and the ram-demon recruit through a self-immolating avatar. She promises each trainee a personalized path for completing a five-part mission whose first task forbids skills, images, and killing.
characters.name: Demigod client

characters.description: The royal target of Raymond and the ram-demon recruit's first field assignment. When they reach her damaged rooms, they discover that another party has already abducted her.
characters.name: Crown princess

characters.description: A small, hostile copy formed when an emotional infection mutates flesh severed from Randidly. It is pulled deeper into the Nexus spine, where stronger time distortion helps it develop control over emotions.
characters.name: Flesh-born imitation

characters.description: The ram-demon trainee previously subjected to image-free field training alongside Raymond. Diortho is learning to rely on physical ability while confronting the dangerous machine-god image that has resisted his control.
characters.name: Diortho

characters.description: The tattooed swordsman who twice hunts Randidly. Veliodun is an ancient killer of rising Nexus talents whose near-perfect cutting image has already destroyed the Fifth Cohort training compound and cost Randidly his left arm.
characters.name: Veliodun

characters.description: An officer responsible for Randidly's recruits during their leader's unexplained absence. Haefel has lost contact with Randidly and must manage the cohort while Commandant Wick demands his return before the Fifth Cohort counteroffensive.
characters.name: Haefel

characters.description: Randidly's separated projected consciousness, left beside his inert body in the Nexus shaft. The Shade protects him while developing a three-layered Nether engraving and searching for a physical medium capable of holding the finished core.
characters.name: Shade

characters.description: An imprisoned Nether gatekeeper who agrees to guard Randidly's inert body after the Shade promises to help it escape from the deep Nexus shaft.
characters.name: Antlered Nether gatekeeper

characters.description: An educator directing the Academy labyrinth on Xperia. Workers identify her as the authority behind the project whose final reward is a massive pillar, a structure the Shade selects as the physical foundation for its Nether core.
characters.name: Gertrude Collins

characters.description: A civic leader helping oversee the Academy labyrinth on Xperia. She discusses its ancient fang reward with Gertrude and believes the world's buried remnants may prove more consequential than the prize currently placed in the labyrinth.
characters.name: Tatiana

characters.description: Raymond recognizes this six-tailed fox as the brother he sought. The fox rejects and gravely injures Raymond, then departs beside an unnamed commander. His remarks expose a thousand-year Nexus effort to tame Nether Kings.
characters.name: Six-tailed fox

recaps.ending: Randidly returns from roughly five subjective years in the Nexus depths after only ten Nexus days. His completed Fang of the Primeval Betrayal protects and conceals Xperia, grants him Weight, and can extend that benefit to connected allies. He rejoins Helen, Nevaeh, Vuala, and the accelerated recruits before the Fifth Cohort counteroffensive. Raymond finds his missing brother, but the six-tailed fox rejects him, mortally wounds him, and departs with an unidentified commander tied to a secret program that has domesticated Nether Kings for a thousand years. Randidly stabilizes Raymond, then uses his identity to join the deployed elite unit. As a Nether King begins folding the moon and the Fifth Cohort together, Commandant Wick blocks the opening ritual. Randidly leads the elites toward an incoming impact zone. Veliodun remains at large, the Aether-consuming structure beneath the Nexus is unexplained, the Labor Council tracker remains in Randidly, and his original teacher holds the next fate piece.
recaps.in_short: Randidly turns two hundred Fifth Cohort recruits into a cohesive elite force while resisting political interference from rival Nexus factions. A hired swordsman, later identified as Veliodun, destroys the training compound, takes Randidly's left arm, and eventually strands him deep inside the Nexus. Extreme time distortion and the Visage of Obsession subject Randidly to years of isolation and escalating sacrifices. His separated Shade completes the Fang of the Primeval Betrayal, a runic Nether core that protects Xperia and grants Weight. Randidly returns after only ten Nexus days, reunites with his allies, and prepares the recruits for war. Raymond finds his missing brother and uncovers a secret program involving domesticated Nether Kings, but is mortally wounded. Randidly saves him, assumes his identity, and covertly leads the elites into the opening Fifth Cohort invasion as Commandant Wick stops the Nether King's first moon-folding ritual.

recaps.text: Previously: Randidly Ghosthound established close working bonds that remain central to his campaign in the Nexus. Helen serves as his veteran lieutenant and trainer, Nevaeh is his soulbound engraving partner, and Vuala is both his offworld partner and a Fifth Cohort combatant. Commandant Wick is his military patron and superior. Randidly's power draws on Aether, Nether, and three principal images, including Yggdrasil, while his ties to Xperia continue across worlds. He enters this volume with allies able to support his military, technical, and personal needs, but those relationships also place obligations on him as the Fifth Cohort faces a growing crisis.

Randidly joins a reform circle planning to use the sealed body of the Nexus creator against the existing order. The plan requires citizenship, military leverage, and engraving research, so he accepts appointment as head drill sergeant for a special Fifth Cohort program. After training in the Nexus web, he claims an unusually large rally-station compound and works with Helen and Nevaeh to build concealed, self-destructing training chambers. Commandant Wick also places Charlotte Wick among the recruits with instructions to cultivate Randidly's loyalty.

Two hundred elite recruits enter a suppression field that forces them to move and fight through their images. Randidly divides them by ability, assigns physical labor and cultivation, and refuses attempts by influential families to interfere. A foxlike recruit enters to find his missing brother and aid his Aether-starved homeworld. The first assessments show a wide gap in image control, but Randidly commits to developing all of them while maintaining the fearsome instructor persona that has grown around him.

The foxlike recruit is identified as Raymond. His nine-tailed-fox image reflects his people's theology, but his instructors find that it lacks a desire of his own. The wider Fifth Cohort emergency rapidly worsens: a rogue Nether King has breached the Nexus Ways, worlds have gone silent, and a Commandant has been killed. Randidly reshapes the elite program for likely frontline service.

Randidly releases Nether through the compound's suppression formation. It circulates among the recruits, strengthening their images and depositing significance, though Raymond suffers its most intense effects. Benjamin Rex recognizes part of the flow pattern. Randidly also introduces Dark Star challenges as an incentive. In the first demonstration, a recruit and five overseers must survive against him for five minutes. Randidly declines to use his own images, overwhelms Helen and the other defenders, and finishes the fight in four seconds. The display establishes the level of danger the recruits are expected to withstand and convinces them to take the training more seriously.

The recruits' shared Nether experience matures one of Randidly's fate pieces and activates the Visage of Obsession, which promises ten compulsory trials with costs. His two hundred elites then defeat about one thousand opposing recruits. Commandant Wick tests Randidly personally and reaches a working political understanding with him, while Military High Command asks the elite squads to become capable of surviving encounters with multiple Nether gatekeepers.

Randidly's growing store of significance threatens a Nether analogue of Aether sickness. Attempts to contact Vuala or study the deep web do not provide a safe solution. Meanwhile, the Nexus Labor Council gains access to the recruits during a funeral leave amid conflict over Aether rationing. Randidly intensifies training but refuses to spy on them. His Grim Chimera evolves under extreme suppression, badly injuring a leading ram-horned recruit who remains too close to the transformation. As the recruits leave for the funeral, Randidly protects Raymond from an aggressive drill sergeant and publicly asserts sole authority over his unit.

At the Commandant's funeral, Randidly encounters a Rex-family woman whose concealed Nether skill surpasses his own. Elsewhere, conspirators attack a Seventh Cohort overseer and manipulate Aether-harvest accounts to frame him. Randidly and his allies turn the falsified records over to Military High Command. A staged confrontation lets the military expose Nexus Labor Council corruption publicly, though its victory depends on withholding Aether from endangered Fifth Cohort worlds. Randidly rejects a Commandant's attempt to influence his emotions and accelerate his power.

Outside deals have compromised several recruits. Randidly destroys a foreign image implanted in one squad leader, then quietly expels the injured host to spare him harsher punishment. Raymond's search for his brother yields only a trail into the Nexus and another disappearance. A ram-demon recruit struggles with a newly strengthened machine-god image, while Raymond still lacks a self-directed purpose. Vuala finally reports from the front that the Nether King's nodes appear to conceal a larger objective. Her brigade has suffered severe losses, and she plans to return briefly to Randidly.

The elite tournaments show rapid improvement, but Raymond and the ram-demon recruit remain divided from their images. Helen assigns them an extended exercise without skills or images. At the next military challenge, an ancient tattooed swordsman ambushes Randidly. His cutting image destroys nearby fighters and overwhelms Randidly's defenses. Randidly saves his people but loses his left arm, suffers damage to his portal key, and watches the training compound collapse before two Commandants force the attacker away.

Vuala returns wounded from the Fifth Cohort, tends to Randidly, and confirms their relationship. Their public spar restores some confidence among the recruits and teaches Randidly more about advanced image development. Raymond and the ram-demon trainee are sent offworld to kidnap a crown princess without killing or using supernatural abilities, only to find another abduction already in progress. Randidly and Vuala later descend into the Nexus web to study the forces near an Aether refinery. The swordsman tracks them there, suppresses Randidly's system access, and confronts him in the depths after Randidly sends Vuala away.

The swordsman springs a prepared trap with two accomplices and drives Randidly deep into the hollow Nexus spine. An ally creates a brief opening, but no rescue can reach him. A hostile emotional infection turns severed flesh into an independent imitation of Randidly. Extreme time distortion gives him months to train while little time passes outside. He eventually descends beyond the point where Nether becomes a unified medium, kills the imitation, and studies its carvings for the first practical clue to a Nether class.

Randidly concludes that engraving adapts a deeper Nether principle and that his class needs a physical core embodying the personal significance of his three images. Nevaeh reaches the Nexus and sends him a replacement-arm design and materials by an engraved spike. Randidly studies deep Nether beasts, learning how their physical cores store power and create lasting stature, but repeated attempts at his own core fail. He activates the Visage of Obsession for a new perspective. Elsewhere, Raymond and his fellow trainee seize the princess from another kidnapper, and Vuala joins their image-free pursuit exercise when Randidly's disappearance extends the mission.

The Visage of Obsession imposes escalating sacrifices. Randidly loses sound, sight, direction, system contact, external connections, and the ability to rest. Each loss narrows his attention while he continues descending and training. He identifies Yggdrasil with stability and growth rooted in his need for support, then spends about a year developing separate layered Nether engravings around each of his three principal images. His incomplete pattern can resist some of the abyssal pull but cannot yet carry him out.

Randidly also forges Nevaeh's design and supplied alloy into a mythic replacement arm able to channel both Aether and Nether. The arm draws hostile emotions and beasts, forcing constant combat. Outside, Vuala and Helen continue Raymond and Diortho's long physical training, while Commandant Wick presses Haefel for Randidly's return before the counteroffensive. Near the bottom of the shaft, an unseen presence disrupts Randidly's tether and consumes his Nether. He begins falling again, prepared to confront whatever created the beast-free voids below.

Porcelain automatons suppress Randidly's images and batter him downward toward a vast prison of Nether gatekeepers and heralds. There he studies their cores and identifies the Grim Chimera's significance as his enduring belief that he can change. The Visage of Obsession then removes his remembered name and demands major internal constructs. His consciousness separates, leaving a Shade beside his inert body to complete the core work.

The Shade promises an antlered Nether gatekeeper escape in return for guarding Randidly's body. It fights upward, gathers objects and memories carrying Randidly's significance, and chooses a pillar from Gertrude Collins's Academy labyrinth on Xperia as the core's physical medium. While pursued by a powerful Nether being, the Shade engraves the pillar and uses the attack to conceal Xperia inside a protective field. Randidly awakens, rescues the gatekeeper under a one-year service agreement, and reunites with the Shade. The System identifies the finished runic Nether sphere as the Fang of the Primeval Betrayal. It protects Xperia through Randidly and grants him Weight.

Randidly returns after experiencing roughly five years away, while the Nexus has advanced by ten days. He reunites with Helen, Nevaeh, Vuala, Raymond, and Diortho. His core can lend Weight to connected allies, and the two recruits have become gatekeeper-capable fighters through accelerated training. Investigators conclude that the structure called an Aether refinery beneath the Nexus actually consumes raw Aether, possibly in connection with something imprisoned below.

The antlered gatekeeper settles among Xperia's dragons and begins seeking a purpose beyond escape. Randidly rebuilds the rally-station defenses and prepares his elite unit for a final public challenge. Rival factions embed veterans among the opposition, but the two hundred elites defeat successive forces numbering in the thousands through coordination and adaptation. When an attacker attempts to kill a defeated elite, Randidly intervenes. Raymond absorbs part of Randidly's pressure and orders the surviving unit to concede before the confrontation becomes open warfare. Randidly heals both sides and leads his recruits away, while Raymond renews his request for help finding his brother.

A Labor Council monitor admits that a high-clearance tracker was placed in Randidly's Aether and offers the location of his next fate piece as restitution. The piece is held by Randidly's original teacher in the Fifth Cohort. Before Randidly can pursue that lead, Raymond follows a six-tailed fox and finds his missing brother. The brother rejects him, inflicts a mortal wound, and leaves with an unidentified commander after revealing a secret Nexus program that has domesticated Nether Kings for a thousand years.

Randidly senses Raymond's collapse, portals to him, and stabilizes his body and soul. At the same time, a Nether King opens a solar-system-scale assault by attempting to fold the moon and the Fifth Cohort together. Commandant Wick blocks the first ritual with his image, but the invasion is underway. Randidly uses Raymond's identification to enter the military muster in his place and rejoins the deployed elite unit covertly. The book ends with Randidly leading the recruits toward an incoming Nether impact zone while warning them that the danger includes forces beyond the visible Nether army.
